transcript.text: The eye area can make or break a face.
Here are two simple steps with the highest return to naturally improve it.
Step one is that most people only focus on the eye color,
but there's something equally important that makes eyes look attractive: clarity and contrast.
It doesn't matter if your eyes are blue, green, or brown.
If your sclera looks yellow or red, the eyes will look tired and less healthy.
That's why one of the oldest tricks is simply using preservative-free eye drops to keep your eyes hydrated and clear.
The second step is to frame your eyes correctly.
Brow shape can heavily influence the perceived tilt of the eyes.
If your canthal tilt is neutral or negative, lifting the outer third of your brow visually extends the tilt upwards.
Brows can also help fix spacing.
If your eyes sit too close, trimming the inner ends widens the gap.
If they sit too far apart, growing the inner ends inwards tightens it.
And finally, you can use your brows to even out asymmetries.
For example, if one eye sits lower than the other, shaping that brow slightly higher visually levels them.
There are dozens of small signals like these that are shaping how your face is perceived.
We break down all of them over at Qoves.com.
